overall_summary: Recent performance data shows strong viewer traction for high-concept space and planetary 'what-if' scenarios, particularly extreme or unusual worlds (e.g., liquid diamond planets, dark planets, burning ice). Engagement metrics (likes-per-view) are notably higher on speculative space scenarios and bizarre cosmic phenomena compared to standard psychological facts or minor biological trivia. Videos utilizing direct hypothetical hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') and rare planetary conditions dominate the top velocity tier over the past 7 days.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) significantly outperform standard factual statements.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical immersion formats where the viewer is placed into impossible or extreme cosmic environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing strange conditions like 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,026 views) capture high view velocity within days of publishing.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight physical impossibilities or bizarre chemical realities on newly discovered or theoretical exoplanets.

weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts focusing on common brain tricks or memory loops (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 5-53 views) show stagnant or negligible view-per-day velocity.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological trivia unless tied to a profound, high-tension narrative twist.
